Parked on branch bl1492-rescue-grid-gate-g1t50-fail (7316da4e). RULED (Ben, 2026-11-04): rescue elsewhere - a refused power rescue tries the next-best non-power recipe before idling; then re-gate. The loss reflex keeps skipping the player's nation (Ben, 2026-11-04: keep the skip), so the gate binds rivals only. RULING (Ben, 2026-11-05): keep parked. Rescue elsewhere on bl1492-rescue-elsewhere (79ff0984) cuts play-built power 71 -> 15 but G1t50 83.6 < 84: floored steel plants refused a power retool idle. Revisit with seed re-curation (BL-1413).

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-05: playtest list and design form)
items.title: A mine costs six months of net at the opening; ease over 10-20 years through reinvestment
items.design: Playtest item 20, Ben's most important. Ruling (Ben, 2026-11-05) in the authority doc. Target: a mine costs about 6 months of a major's net at the opening, back to about 1 month after 10-20 years; 6x in 15 years is about 13% a year, or roughly an 8-year payback on a good building. Cost lives mostly in materials, so a planned steel chain is the edge. Good sites pay back in years, poor ones barely: the finder stays open (Ben declined gating it), so this spread is the WHOLE reward for searching and must be read, not assumed. Calibrate from the payback census; multipliers are in-band. RISKS: raises steel demand and can stretch or pause sites (max_stretch); rivals barely build today (median 44 to about 47 in five years), so read whether they stall further; read against BL-1494 (tick-50 stall). Check: market-viability, opening-parity, rebless-shape-probe. One re-bless shared with the other world-movers. CALIBRATION from the census (BL-1496): six months of net at the measured 1,000-1,150 a quarter is a mine of about 2,000-2,300, about 5-6x today's 327-430. Reinvestment grows income at 1/payback whatever the net: a x5.5 mine pays back in about 5 years on produce (0.9 today), 9 on copper, 21 on iron, 40 on coal; standing processors in about 15-25 years. Background growth of about 4.7% a year carries about 2.5x of the 6x over 20 years, leaving about 2.4x for reinvestment, so x5-6 looks feasible and must be run, not assumed. Timber, fibre and stone mines cost about 105-110 today with no steel in the bill: the materials lever must reach them. Read net after research: see the review queue.

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-05: playtest follow-up)
items.title: Construction tooltip warns when a building's supply has only a few quarters left on the shelf
items.design: Ben, 2026-11-05: "warnings on tooltip for construction when a building's supply has only a few quarters left on that market's stockpile". READING, to confirm: a building's supply means its recipe inputs at the tile's market. For each input: shelf (market inventory) over the quarterly use this building would add, plus that market's net drain where it is already falling. Under the threshold, the Build door row's tooltip (selection_panel.cpp near :4818) names the good and the quarters left; the site ledger's row carries the same reading from one shared helper. OPEN: the threshold (4 quarters as the default until Ben reads it live), and whether construction materials count too. It serves the search reward in PRODUCTION § What construction costs at the opening: it shows a site that looks profitable today but will starve. The word on screen is shelf (GLOSSARY). UI only. Check: live click, question log.

items.author: main session (BL-1496 census, 2026-11-05)
items.title: The door and the site finder quote what a plant can actually run on
items.design: Found by BL-1496 (build payback census). The door and the finder pass nullptr for input_unit_cost, pricing inputs at the posted price with a full run, so the top rows are goods whose inputs are not there: alloys quoted 4,669 earned 615, electronics 2,332 earned -6. A player trusting the finder is burned, and Ben's ruling rests the whole search reward on these sites (he kept the finder open). The rival scorer already prices through input_reach (BL-1187); the player's quote should use the same obtainable cost plus an expected run from the shelf. That should also open the spread processing lacks (1.1x today), since obtainable cost varies by site: measure it. This is a figure, not a rule, so no sim digest moves if the scorer's call stays byte-identical. Check: census ACTUAL rows, quoted within about 2x of earned on the mirage rows; best-over-median spread for processing reported; live click. Pairs with SHELF_RUNWAY_WARNING. READING 2026-11-06, 16 library seeds, 40 quarters, holdout of 549 processors quoted when ordered and read a year after standing: median |quote - earned| 46.6 old, 24.8 new; right about whether it pays 80% old, 87% new; called idle 58, of which 7 ran above half; extractors steel-free timber 59.5 old, 9.6 new, earned 4.7. Rejected on the same holdout: the scorer's spare-supply test (131 called idle, 95 ran). KNOWN MISS: consumer goods median earned -4.2, quoted 378 (was 4,629), run 0 with inputs apparently available: not explained by the shelf or the bid. The Method lever at selection_panel.cpp:793 still prices at posted.

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-05: "Yes, count research", NR-1143)
items.title: Research counts inside the quarterly return, so NET is the money left
items.design: Ben's ruling, in FINANCE § The quarterly return: research counts inside net. Today nation_tech.cpp:1059 takes it from the treasury after the return is written, a mean of 1,644 credits a major-quarter by BL-1496 (build payback census), against net of 1,000-2,500, so NET overstates free cash. Book it as refunds are booked: a running figure the nation step adds to, drained into the next return, with the return's opening taken so net still telescopes. Check garrison pay at nation_step.cpp:349 at the same time: any other direct spend outside the return makes NET lie the same way, and the census's resid column should read zero after this. quarterly_return is asserted sizeof 56 and hashed raw, so it is a save bump and moves the return digest: goes in the ECONOMY wave's shared re-bless. Do before BL-1497 (opening cost curve) sets the mine at six months of net, since that target now reads net after research. Check: census resid near zero; the retain property (returns replay onto the treasury) still holds; save round trip.

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-05: sprint 64 naval design form)
items.title: Measure how much trade crosses water, per seed and per nation, before any raid number is set
items.design: MEASURE FIRST. Raiding and blockade are worth only what crosses the water. Per library seed and per major: the share of landed cargo value on a sea leg, the same for a nation's imports, and how many ports carry it. Goldens cannot see trade, so this is a harness reading on the shipped start. If the share is small, that is a finding to raise with Ben before patrol, escort and raid are tuned. Run after sprint 63's economy wave. Patrol, escort and raid were built ahead of this reading, on a first-cut raid_take_permille_per_day of 100: in the harness field one raider takes about 97% of whole crossings. Read that against real lanes here and tune in BL-1535 (naval war reading).

items.title: A major opens with the fixed fleet of its kit, berthed from its capital port
items.design: MILITARY.md § Sea, "A major's opening fleet is fixed" (Ben, 2026-11-07); NATION_GENERATION.md, "History leaves no fleet"; CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § A major's opening kit. The kit authors the ships (all four classes in fixed shares), the berths per port and the sea pool. The kit's one-port cap must keep a sea-mouthed port where the major holds one, so the fleet has a berth (Ben, 2026-11-07: prefer the sea, inside this item). A world-mover: measure before and after, and land it in the sprint's one re-bless.

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-05: sprint 64 naval design form)
items.title: Rival nations raise ships and assign every mission by the scorer
items.design: AI_OPPONENT.md § 11, the fleet grant. Hire, design, mission and landing verbs through corp_command, and no reading of undetected ships. A sunk cargo must score above zero or a rival submarine never raids. Validate each new verb as an untrusted input at the seam. The next-verb bound applies: an invasion is a sequence of separately scored verbs, so measure whether rivals actually land. The research scorer has no notion of ships or ports: it counts w.units only and pays ship kit per row with no port test, so a landlocked rival buys Naval kit late and uses none. Whether it may read a nation's own ships and ports is part of this grant; raise it.

items.design: v0.3.0 needs the naval system and a playtest with a few wars. Sweep the library: fleets raised, raids landed, ports closed, landings made, treasuries under fleet upkeep. Then the sprint's one re-bless, described by rebless_shape_probe, ruling-check, and a live war played to a landing. It also owes the one reading the blockade could not show on a fixture: a clearing price moving at a blockaded market on a real seed. It also owes a landed army on a real seed: its stocks running down with no port, and holding once it takes one.

items.title: Wages are a flat bill on the treasury, and ship and air crews draw them
items.design: MILITARY.md § What a force costs. run_nation_garrison_upkeep stops taking its share from the military_research weight: the whole bill is owed, paid from the treasury as far as it goes, and a short payment weakens every unit, wing and ship by the one decay rule. items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-08: force sizing and pay forms)
items.title: A rival sizes land, air and sea to its income and its neighbours, replacing the caps of three
items.design: MILITARY.md § Force sizing; AI_OPPONENT.md § 11 grant of 2026-11-08. One pass computes running cost, income, target share with threat, the shortfall share of uncommitted treasury and the split by position, then hires at most one per theatre an evaluation through the legal verbs. Retires k_rival_wing_cap and k_rival_ship_cap, and restores land hiring for nations. A census reads forces against income over the seed library before any number is settled.
